description: DUBLD is a database of geometric and thermophysical properties for about 28,000 buildings in Dublin city centre, Ireland, between the canals, an area of about 15 square kilometres, prepared so that the whole district can be modelled for building energy. It was published on Zenodo on 21 March 2023 by Niall Buckley. For each building it gives a unique identifier, height, floor area, estimated year of construction and use, U-values for roofs, walls, floors, windows and doors (with second and third values where a building has several types), window-to-wall ratio, facade description, length and area, glazing type, and coefficients of performance for oil and gas boilers. Access: a zip file of about 1.4 MB with a metadata spreadsheet, openly downloadable. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: construction years, uses and thermal properties are estimates, assigned by archetype, not surveyed for every building. Simulation uses are urban building energy modelling, district heating planning and retrofit scenarios for the city centre. Related records: archetypal and the England and Wales EPC data.
